failures.criterion: A1 / spec Summary: a comment, ask, message or reply holding a (finished) mermaid code block shows a drawn diagram
failures.evidence: A closed mermaid fence followed by a link reference definition never draws. A link definition is no block of the parse, so the diagram is the document's last leaf block, while `endsInOpenMermaidFence` (packages/dispatch/web/src/features/refs/mermaid-diagrams.ts:78-83) reads the source's last line, `[spec]: https://example.com/spec`, as no closing fence and drops the block as 'still streaming'. Real surface: a throwaway Playwright run (chromium, tester lane) with a comment `Ref def after:` + ```mermaid graph TD X --> Y``` + `[spec]: https://example.com/spec` -> 0 images named 'Rendered Mermaid diagram', the source visible as code (screenshot /legion/scratch/tmp/tester-probe-refdef.png); the same diagram without the definition draws. Red test: `a closed mermaid fence followed by a link reference definition draws its diagram` in packages/dispatch/web/src/features/refs/MarkdownBody.test.tsx (commit 313753db), shown failing by `cd packages/dispatch && bun test web/src/features/refs/MarkdownBody.test.tsx -t Mermaid` -> Expected length: 1, Received length: 0.

failures.criterion: Plan: a mermaid block whose fence is still open (a streamed live-view turn) stays code and never flashes a refusal
failures.evidence: `CLOSING_FENCE` (mermaid-diagrams.ts:48) accepts any 3+ backticks or tildes as the last line, but CommonMark closes a fence only with the opener's character at least as long as the opener. A body ending in ````` ````mermaid ... ``` ````` (four-backtick opener, the stream at three) or ```` ```mermaid ... ~~~ ```` is still open, yet draws. Red test: `a body ending in a line that cannot close its mermaid fence keeps it as code` in MarkdownBody.test.tsx (commit 313753db), failing with the same command -> Expected length: 1, Received length: 2. A fix that compares the last line with the block's own opening fence also fixes the first failure.
